# AGENTS.md rule 10 points at ADR-0019, which now lives in the Brain repository

### The problem

`AGENTS.md` rule 10 is a hard mandate that points at a file which is no longer in this repository:

> 10. **No AiConfig work without reading ADR-0019 first.** Before authoring OR reviewing ANY `ai/` config touch, read `learn/agentos/decisions/0019-aiconfig-reactive-provider-ssot.md` — no exception, no approval signal, no CI-green substitute …

`learn/agentos/decisions/0019-aiconfig-reactive-provider-ssot.md` was removed on 2026-08-27 in `c623b2f63`, *feat(engine): remove received Brain implementation (#17791) (#17806)*. The surviving ADRs in `learn/agentos/decisions/` are `0004`, `0007`, `0008`, `0018` and `0020`.

The ADR itself is alive, in the Brain repository: `learn/agentos/decisions/0019-aiconfig-reactive-provider-ssot.md` [QUARANTINED_URL: github.com] on `dev`.

### Why it matters

The rule says "no exception". An agent that obeys it tries to read a path that does not resolve, and rule 10 is specifically the one whose text argues that diligence alone has already failed twice (`#12420`, `#14499`). A dead pointer on that particular rule is the worst place for one.

`.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`, so it carries the same line and one edit fixes both.

### Proposed fix

Repoint the reference at the Brain repository, in the same style `CONTRIBUTING.md` already uses for Strategic Workflows [QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]. One line, `AGENTS.md` only.

If you would rather the ADR came back into this repo, or rule 10 is now obsolete along with the received Brain implementation, say which and I will follow that instead.

### How this was found

I run a checker that resolves every path cited in a repository's agent and contributor docs against that repository's git history, so a deletion or rename surfaces as drift. Two other hits on this repo were **not** real and I am recording them so nobody re-reports them: `.agents/skills/identity-firewall/audits/channel-separation.md` and `.agents/skills/session-sunset/SKILL.md` are absent from git only because `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills/` are gitignored and materialized from the `neo-agent-skills` npm dependency by its `postinstall`. They resolve fine in a working install.

Per CONTRIBUTING §5: this issue and the accompanying fix were prepared with an AI agent, Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed the result and I am accountable for it.
